reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only describes HEA coatings on Q235 substrates and their corrosion resistance; it provides no data on the microstructure, oxide film formation, or corrosion behavior of untreated Q235 steel itself. The key premises about Q235's inherent heterogeneity and its mechanistic link to corrosion are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Microstructural heterogeneity (grain boundaries, inclusions) in Q235 causes nonuniform iron oxide films
Nonuniform oxide films create local electrochemical potential gradients that initiate localized corrosion
Thermal annealing homogenizes Q235 microstructure and reduces potential gradients
Homogenized Q235 forms a more uniform, adherent, and protective oxide layer
This mechanism applies in chloride-rich environments at room and moderately elevated temperatures
